clips.verdict: Dead on arrival at 0 views after 116h; a reading-aloud premise with a vague hook, and too old to judge on anything but distribution.
clips.worked: The narrator line is a clean one-sentence premise (a fan read a whole book on seduction to write this letter), and the fan-mail format is spoken, so it works without visuals.
clips.hurt: The hook 'WAIT FOR HIS LIFE ADVICE' is the vague tease we banned, and it promises a payoff the narrator never sets up. 53s is far too long for one letter gag. The title's 'Art Of Seduction' is trivia rather than a question the clip answers.
clips.better_title: Jynxzi Gets a Fan Letter From a Seduction Book Fan 📚😭
clips.better_hook: HE READ A WHOLE BOOK FOR THIS

clips.verdict: Weak pick: fans chasing Kai is visual crosstalk with no spoken premise, so it was unlikely to land even with distribution.

clips.verdict: Best premise of the batch (a guessing-game joke with a spoken payoff), but the result is in the title and it ran 53s.
clips.worked: The narrator line is a good setup and payoff: 'promised to overestimate everyone, lasted one gamertag'. The rank-guessing format is a spoken premise that is funny read aloud.
clips.hurt: The title gives away the result ('Copper'). The hook 'HE JUDGED HIM BEFORE THE CLIP' is a mood tease that doesn't state a stake. The narrator already delivers the punchline, so the clip pays off before it starts. At 164h it competes with hundreds of other Jynxzi clippers.

clips.verdict: Right kind of pick (Speed vs a celebrity athlete with a stated stake) and the only clip with any views (15), but the execution gave away the best part.
clips.worked: A bet with a stake ('whole stream on the line') is exactly the premise the breakouts use. The hook 'HE SWORE HE'D END THE STREAM' is close to a stake. Speed and Palmer is a strong crossover.
clips.hurt: The title spoils the outcome ('Red Card'). The narrator's 'and then this happened' is the banned filler. 53s dilutes the bet-to-payoff gap. 169h old, so it missed the window when Speed and Palmer content was fresh.
clips.better_title: Speed Bets His Whole Stream Against Cole Palmer ⚽😭

clips.verdict: Visual clinch with no spoken premise, so there was nothing for a scroller to wait for.
clips.worked: The narrator's joke ('decided boxing was hugging now') is funny and the Adin boxing event has built-in audience interest.

titles: Creator name first, then the setup in plain verbs, with no result in the title (Red Card, Copper, Hang On all gave it away).
Write the title as the question or bet the clip answers, e.g. 'Asks If This Dog Is Ever Happy'. Never use trivia like 'Japan's Most Popular Dog'.
hooks: Max 6 words, stated as a stake or question the clip answers within 15s. Cut vague teases like 'WAIT FOR HIS LIFE ADVICE'.
Hook and narrator must not say the same thing. Let the narrator set up the premise and the hook add the stake, or cut one.
clip_picks: Only cut moments with a one-line spoken premise (bet, guess, countdown, question). Speed and Kai crossovers with athletes or celebrities come first, then Kai with Ray.
Skip visual-only moments such as fans chasing Kai, a clinch, or a dog. If the transcript isn't funny read aloud, skip it.
Jynxzi guessing ranks is a repeatable spoken format worth mining, but only when the premise is stated up front.
length_and_pacing: Stop cutting every clip to 53s. Start ≤2s before the stake line and end ≤2s after the payoff. Aim for 15-30s, since the breakouts are mostly 11-26s.
End on the payoff line and cut trailing banter so the clip loops cleanly.
posting: Post 1-2 clips a day within hours of the stream. Clips 5-7 days old compete with hundreds of other clippers.
All six clips sit at 0-15 views with n/a analytics, which points to distribution, not just picks. Check Studio for limits, duplicate-content flags and Shorts-feed serving before judging any clip.
After 48h, judge on 3s retention and Shorts-feed share, but only once Studio shows those numbers.

money.why: N3on is the one known campaign, and your format (short cuts of streamer moments) is what these campaigns pay for. It earns without needing 1,000 subs or 10M Shorts views.
money.first_step: Read N3on's campaign rules (allowed sources, length, payout metric) and cut 2-3 compliant clips this week, tracking views per clip.

money.idea: Long-form or compilation videos for the YPP long-form route
money.why: The Shorts view thresholds (3M and 10M) are far from 18 views. Compilations of the same streamer moments can build subs and watch hours on a different path.
money.first_step: Check the YPP long-form requirements in Studio, then assemble one 8-10 minute compilation of the best spoken-premise moments once you have a few that work.

money.idea: Affiliate links in the description once there is an audience
money.why: Fan-funding and ad share are both locked at 0 subs. Affiliate links need no YPP, but only pay once there is traffic.
money.first_step: Hold until a clip passes a few thousand views, then add one relevant affiliate link (e.g. capture or editing gear you actually use) to the description.

next_actions: Open Studio and check the channel for limits, duplicate-content or reused-content flags, and whether Shorts are being served in the feed. Everything here is 0-15 views, which points to distribution.
Join the N3on campaign if the terms fit, and cut 2-3 compliant clips as the first revenue test.
Cut only fresh moments (posted within hours of the stream) with a spoken premise: Speed or Kai with a celebrity or athlete, then Kai with Ray.
Recut at 15-30s with a ≤6-word stake hook, and drop 'and then this happened' from narrator lines.
Check 3s retention and Shorts-feed share in Studio after 48h on the next batch before judging picks.
